system.name: S-ViLM
system.one_liner: Video-language pre-training with a dual encoder plus temporal grouping, spatial grounding of nouns to learnable group tokens, and global contrastive learning.

content.variant_note: a two-column dual-encoder diagram whose token rows feed three objectives; two dotted-frame insets above show attract and repel on real frames
content.argues: Group tokens that bind video regions to caption nouns, and a cut-and-paste foreground versus background signal, add fine-grained structure to instance-level video-text contrast.
content.subject: A video side and a text side producing tokens, three training objectives on those tokens, and two insets showing temporal repel and spatial attract and repel.

encoding.color_means: light blue = video side; pale orange = text side; purple, amber, red and teal = four group tokens, with purple, amber and red repeated on the noun tokens, on the nouns man, bowling ball and pins and on the matching image regions; blue dashed frames = background clip and its tokens; red dashed frames = foreground clip and its tokens
encoding.line_style_means: dotted frame = an objective inset; dashed frame = a group of tokens or a clip; long dashed arrows = this token set is what that objective acts on; solid arrows = data flow; double-headed arrows labelled Attract or Repel = pull or push in the loss
encoding.shape_means: rounded square = a video or group token; oval = a text token; hatched blue square = a token of the background clip; wide rounded box = an encoder
encoding.marker_means: the words Attract and Repel on arrows give the sign of the loss; the plus sign means the pasted clip is added onto the background clip
encoding.emphasis: One colour per object runs through region, group token, noun token and noun, so the correspondence being learned reads at a glance; the new objectives sit in titled insets above the main diagram.

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each concept one colour and carry it through every representation (image region, learnable token, text token, word in the caption) so the correspondence being learned reads at a glance; put the objectives as titled dotted-frame insets above the main dual-encoder diagram and tie them to the token rows with long dashed arrows.
lessons.suits: Multimodal pre-training with several auxiliary objectives, each explained by pulls and pushes between colour-coded tokens.

evidence: temporal grouping learns temporal-aware features by distinguishing whether clips are from background or foreground
the red region corresponds exactly to the word “pins” in red

summary: S-ViLM is a video-language pre-training framework that adds structure to the usual dual encoder with intra-clip temporal grouping, inter-clip spatial grounding and global contrastive learning. Figure 1 draws the main diagram in two columns: an input bowling clip goes through Cut & Paste and a Video Encoder, with four learnable group tokens, to video tokens and group tokens; an input caption goes through a Text Encoder, with Noun Extraction & Prompting, to a caption token and noun tokens; both sides meet at Contrastive Learning. Above it, two dotted-frame insets show the new objectives: foreground and background clip tokens repel, and group tokens attract their matching nouns, all colour-coded.
summary_zh: S-ViLM 在双编码器视频语言预训练上加入时间分组、空间对齐和全局对比三个目标。下方是视频与文本两栏主流程，上方两个点线框说明前景背景相斥、区域与名词相吸，并用同色贯穿。
notes: The two dotted insets are recorded as the panels; the main two-column drawing is unframed and acts as the base, hence arrangement inset. The hatched blue squares in the token rows are small bitmaps. That blue dashed frames mean background and red dashed frames mean foreground is read from the figure and the caption (distinguishing background from foreground clips); the colours themselves are not keyed.
